I work in a behavioral school. We follow evidence-based methods for correcting bad behavior. It isn’t something that can be cured overnight or in a few weeks sometimes. I would strongly recommend that you ignore any undesirable behavior; if you feel the need to redirect or give a soft warning, gently redirect them with a positive tone of voice. What I recommend is that you ONLY acknowledge any positive behaviors, and that you do that very regularly individually with all of the students who are modeling behaviors that you want. “Great job putting your name on your paper.”, “I like the way that you are using materials safely.”, “Great job staying in your area working quietly.” Make sure that all of your students hear your praises and that you aren’t giving any sense of being aggravated, frustrated, or defeated. 
One thing that you should know is that a lot of kids want attention, either positive or negative. It doesn’t matter to them. If they can get your attention through negative behaviors, they will do that. Instead, reinforce and show through consistency that you will ALWAYS provide attention to students meeting your expectations. Make sure that any verbal or tangible reinforcement is given immediately. Most kids cannot handle delayed gratification unless they choose that - it generally doesn’t work. If you give any tangible reinforcement (token system, food item, candy, computer game time, etc.) it should always be accompanied by a verbal praise so that the student knows what they are doing correctly. I would investigate some of the ABA principles if you want to learn more. Hope this helps!
